parameters.primerDisplay: Uniformly compressed; positions 1, 2, 17 and 18 are shown with a break mark. Physical length remains 18 nt.

scientificConstraints: One type of sequencing primer; many identical template copies.
Dye identity follows terminal ddNTP base; identical terminal bases repeat colors.
Products are pedagogically displayed in increasing length order; actual terminators incorporate stochastically.
A terminal dd residue has no 3-prime OH and cannot resume extension.
Incoming nucleotide triphosphate releases pyrophosphate upon incorporation; the strand retains one phosphate.
Only single-strand extension products are loaded after cleanup and denaturation.
Fragments carry negative charge and migrate upward toward the positive electrode; short fragments travel further.
The aligned fragment panel is a synthesis record after loading, not a second physical aliquot.
A fluorescent band represents many fragments of the same length; colors are fluorescence detection pseudocolors.
Contemporary instruments commonly use capillary electrophoresis; this gel is a teaching representation.
The five-membered sugar ring contains O4-prime and four carbons; C5-prime is outside the ring, linked toward the phosphate. Base attachment is at C1-prime.
The same primer display compression applies to all products and the template; only the 12-base measured region uses full uniform spacing.
An external C5-prime label identifies the carbon between the ring C4-prime and the phosphate chain.
The whole-terminator glow and violet sugar are visual cues; the single fluorescent dye remains linked on the base side.
A dashed vertical guide marks the common primer 3-prime boundary where measured extension begins.
